steps.text: Adjust the risk controls, pick a mode and practise on the demo before going live.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
redFlags: A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.
Ownership details missing from the public pages.
The demo promised in the pitch but buried in the flow.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.
9 crypto assets through broker partners, per the published pages. The list varies between sections, so check the dashboard after signup.

bottomLine: The desk, the demo and the funding options all check out. The score reflects the paperwork around them.
The verdict holds at 4.5: research it, demo it, and if you fund it, fund the minimum. The platform earns a careful start, not blind trust.
